locator.section: 8.2 Product stability -- Charge competition in OE(+.) decompositions: Stevenson's Rule

evidence.curator_note: Eq 8.3 row 2, second branch, arrow labeled 'alpha'. Radical-site (alpha) cleavage driven by the ether oxygen radical cation: the odd electron on O5 forms the new C4=O5 pi bond (methoxymethylene oxocarbenium CH2=O(+)-CH3, m/z 45) while the C3-C4 sigma bond breaks and the propyl group departs as the neutral radical .C3H7. The printed IE for forming this resonance-stabilized cation is 6.9 eV, far below IE(C3H7.)=8.1 eV, so per Stevenson's rule charge migration to the oxocarbenium overwhelmingly wins (100% vs the 4% C3H7+ inductive branch 8.3c). Book draws 0 arcs (summary equation); the three fishhooks (O5 odd electron -> C4=O5 pi; one electron of the C3-C4 bond -> the same pi; the second electron of that bond -> the departing propyl radical) are the standard balanced radical-site alpha-cleavage flow, reconstructed here. DELOCALIZATION: CH2=O(+)-CH3 is the oxocarbenium resonance form of (+)CH2-O-CH3; the double-bonded form is the one encoded.

Cross-linked MOD rule IMS_8_3_alpha (equation 8.3). It correctly cleaves the C-C bond and forms the CH2=O(+) oxocarbenium, matching this alpha branch on the ion side; BUT it simultaneously emits the propyl fragment as a cation C3H7(+) rather than the neutral radical .C3H7, so its RHS carries charge +2 -- charge-non-conserving and dropped by the conservation guardrail. The alpha bond change (form C4=O5, break C3-C4) matches this record; the charge/spin bookkeeping does not. See rule_mismatches.

Book prints '100%' relative abundance under CH2=OCH3+ (base of this competition). observed_mz 45.0335 is the curator-computed electron-mass-corrected monoisotopic m/z of C2H5O+; the page prints only the % abundance and the fragment IE (6.9 eV), no m/z.
